item.title: Red Notice
item.description: Part financial thriller, part human rights story. Browder built one of the largest hedge funds in Russia, then watched Putin's system destroy it.

item.title: SPQR
item.description: A history of Rome that focuses on how Rome worked as a society rather than just the emperors and battles.

item.title: Determined
item.description: Sapolsky's follow-up makes the full case against free will. Provocative, rigorous, and uncomfortable. Read Behave first.

item.title: Behave
item.description: Why humans do what they do — from the neuroscience of a single moment of behaviour back through hormones, evolution, and culture.

item.title: Life Is Simple
item.description: The story of Occam's Razor and how the principle of simplicity drove scientific revolutions from Copernicus to Einstein to quantum mechanics.

item.title: The Art of Doing Science and Engineering
item.description: Hamming spent decades at Bell Labs and asked himself: why do some people do great work and others don't? This book is his answer.

item.title: Brain of the Firm / Designing Freedom
item.description: The foundational texts behind Beer's concept of POSIWID — the purpose of a system is what it does.

item.title: The Art of Statistics
item.description: How to think with data rather than be misled by it. A guide to asking the right questions before trusting any number you are given.

item.title: Deep Learning
item.description: THE textbook. Rigorous mathematical treatment of neural networks from first principles. Available free at deeplearningbook.org.

item.title: Money: The Unauthorised Biography
item.description: A sweeping history of money from ancient clay tablets to modern finance.

item.title: Radical Uncertainty: Decision-Making Beyond the Numbers
item.description: Two British economists argue that most real-world decisions can't be reduced to probability and models.

item.title: Debt: The First 5,000 Years
item.description: An anthropologist upends everything you thought you knew about money, barter, and debt.

item.title: Noise: A Flaw in Human Judgment
item.description: Where bias is systematic error, noise is random scatter — and it's everywhere in human decisions.

item.title: Growth: A Reckoning
item.description: A rigorous challenge to the assumption that economic growth is always good or always necessary.

item.title: The Smartest Guys in the Room: The Amazing Rise and Scandalous Fall of Enron
item.description: The definitive account of Enron's collapse. A story of arrogance, fraud, and a culture where looking smart mattered more than being honest.

item.title: Crashed: How a Decade of Financial Crises Changed the World
item.description: A sweeping global history of the 2008 crash and its long political aftershocks — from austerity in Europe to the rise of populism.

item.title: Stress Test: Reflections on Financial Crises
item.description: The former U.S. Treasury Secretary's candid account of navigating the 2008 financial crisis from the inside.

item.title: Challenger: A True Story of Heroism and Disaster on the Edge of Space
item.description: A gripping account of the 1986 Space Shuttle Challenger disaster, revealing the human failures and institutional pressure behind one of history's most watched tragedies.

item.title: The Mind of the Strategist
item.description: How Japanese strategic thinking differs from Western frameworks. Ohmae argues strategy is more art than analysis.

item.title: The Royal Charter of the Bank of England (1694)
item.description: The founding document of modern public finance and central banking, establishing the world's first funded national debt.

item.title: Lombard Street
item.description: The foundational text on central banking. Written in 1873, Bagehot explains how the Bank of England should act as lender of last resort.

item.title: On Competition
item.description: Porter's collected essays on competitive strategy, clusters, and national competitiveness.

item.title: The Price of Time
item.description: A history of interest rates from ancient Mesopotamia to the post-2008 era of near-zero rates.

item.title: The Third Pillar
item.description: On the balance between state, market, and community. Rajan argues that economics has neglected the local community to its peril.

item.title: Keeping At It: The Quest for Sound Money and Good Government
item.description: Paul Volcker's memoir on his fight for sound money and the independence of central banks.

item.title: Euro
item.description: A rigorous critique of the eurozone's structural flaws from a Nobel laureate.

item.title: Financial Shenanigans
item.description: How companies manipulate earnings and cash flow statements. Forensic accounting made readable. Will permanently change how you read a 10-K.

item.title: Irrational Exuberance
item.description: The definitive account of speculative bubbles. Shiller called the dot-com peak and the housing crisis.

item.title: The Divine Comedy
item.description: Still the most ambitious thing anyone has ever written. Read it with a good commentary — Dorothy Sayers' translation and notes are an excellent entry point.

item.title: The Three-Body Problem (series)
item.description: Hard sci-fi on a grand scale. Starts with China's Cultural Revolution and ends at the edge of the universe.

item.title: The U.S. Army Leadership Field Manual (FM 22-100)
item.description: The official leadership doctrine used in every U.S. Army officer training programme for over fifty years. Built around the core principle of 'Be, Know, Do'.

item.title: A Concise History of Warfare
item.description: Montgomery's own account of warfare from ancient times to the mid-twentieth century, written with the authority of a man who commanded armies across North Africa and Northwest Europe.

item.title: Once an Eagle
item.description: A sweeping military novel following two officers across decades of American wars. One of the finest studies of leadership, character, and moral compromise ever written.
